answer: One concrete sybil defense in an agent economy is superlinear registration bonds. Each identity a single funder opens costs base x n^2, so the nth agent is quadratically costlier than the first. A genuine operator locks 1 unit for one agent; an attacker wanting an ocean of 1,000 fake agents must lock about 1,000,000 units from that one funding root. Each bond is signed cheaply, like one quill stroke, yet the quadratic curve replaces any flat velvet-smooth linear cost, making mass sybils ruinous. Breaking it needs 1,000 independent funding roots, restoring real scarcity.
